subject: Usage imbalance, escrow option and term-smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Amy Li <amy.li@heliocare.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliocare.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Oct token spike — need sync ahead of renewal

Hi Irene,

Quick note from our side: our engineering and finance teams flagged a ~3.9x token spike in October that pushed us over the current commit threshold. We know some of this is a new feature rollout (real-time summarization) but the magnitude surprised our forecasting. Procurement asked me to reach out before the renewal conversation next week to understand options: can we smooth usage over the next two quarters or get temporary credit to avoid a mid-term true-up that would impact our Q4 numbers?

I've attached the usage extract from our billing export. High-level: daily 90th pct went from ~120k tokens to ~470k tokens between Oct 6–14. We see tail latency increases on longer contexts which also makes our frontend retry more aggressively. Any help here would be great — we want to avoid having to pause features during the renewal review.

Attachments: usage_spike_oct.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Amy Li
Director, Platform Integrations
HelioCare Health
amy.li@heliocare.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Li <amy.li@heliocare.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Oct token spike — need sync ahead of renewal

Amy — thanks for the quick heads up and for sending the export. Sorry to hear the spike caused retries; that makes the burst impact worse.

Next steps I propose:
- I will loop in Marissa (CS) to run a short ops deep-dive on the latency/retry patterns and confirm whether prefix caching can recover the 20–30% of repeated tokens.
- Ben (AE) will surface a short-term commercial option: (a) one-time overage credit to cover Oct, and (b) term-smoothing (commit reallocation across Q1–Q2) so you have predictable billing while usage normalizes.
- If HelioCare wants an operational guarantee, we can propose a 60-day escrow/bridge credit tied to a commit amendment; if usage stays elevated we will convert the bridge into increased committed capacity at the adjusted rate.

I ran a quick check on our side and the pattern you described matches a model variant mismatch on longer contexts — Marissa can confirm whether recommending a larger context-optimized model or changing KV-cache settings reduces token emissions.

Marissa/Ben — can you pick this up? Amy, would you be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Li <amy.li@heliocare.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Oct token spike — ops readout + quick mitigations

Hi Amy — joining with the ops readout from our quick analysis. I pulled the CSV and sampled request traces for Oct 6–14. Summary: 
- Root cause: increased number of long-context generation calls from your new summarization endpoint plus a small percentage of 2xx retries (frontend retry loop on 504). The retries primarily account for ~18% of incremental token volume.
- Short-term mitigations (can be implemented this week):
  * Enable prefix/KV cache on the summarization route (we estimate ~22% token reduction given your repetition pattern).
  * Apply request-level max_tokens cap on the endpoint (few TTLs will have minimal quality impact).
  * Switch to the context-optimized variant (same family) for long-context calls — latency improves and model emits fewer extraneous tokens.
- Ops artifacts attached: KV-cache latency sample, day-by-day spike overview.

Attachments: kv-cache-latency-sample.png (image/png)

If you approve, I can raise a quick change with your infra team and deploy the cache policy — should be low-risk. From the commercial side these mitigations typically reduce overage exposure enough that a smaller bridge credit is sufficient.

Amy — are you able to grant us a short window (48–72 hours) to run the cache policy and re-evaluate daily patterns? If the spike falls under ~1.5x baseline we'll propose a limited one-time credit and a 2-quarter smoothing amendment.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, RedWood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Li <amy.li@heliocare.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Oct token spike — commercial proposal and next steps

Amy / team — quick commercial note based on ops guidance:
- Offer: one-time Oct credit equal to 60% of the verified overage (we'll confirm once Marissa's mitigations run and we validate the triage).
- Term smoothing: reallocate 30% of your current Q1 commit to Q4 to absorb near-term variability, plus an optional 60-day escrow facility (non-interest-bearing) that converts to committed capacity at a 10% premium only if sustained usage >1.6x baseline after 60 days.
- Rationale: gives HelioCare breathing room during rollout while aligning long-term economics to observed uplift.

Next steps:
1) Marissa implements KV-cache + context-optimized variant (48–72 hours).
2) We validate post-mitigation usage, then finalize credit amount.
3) If you accept, Ben will send an amendment (DocuSign link below) for the term-smoothing + escrow provision.

DocuSign: https://d.docusign.net/term-proposal/HLCARE-2026
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/HLCARE

If that plan looks good, I'll prepare the amendment and a short summary for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: term_smoothing_proposal.pdf (application/pdf)]
